summary: Tested the Replay option on the Accept/Decline pop-up (backend + UI), saving replayMessage, Quick IVR code calls with Replay in preview, the extension row layout and the light-theme code colour. The main features all pass. Also tried Emily (optional): the Spanish voicemail sub-menu and key 4 smsFrom are correct, but she still adds after-hours lines nobody asked for.

minor.issue: Asked 'add a Spanish option on key 9 that takes a voicemail'. The reply still had the summary line 'After hours menu: disabled', the missing note 'The after-hours menu only plays once your Hours schedule is on (Hours tab).' and an 'After-hours menu' chip. Cause: the frontend sends current.afterHours = {enabled:false, greeting:'', greetingAudioUrl:null, options:[]}, but clean()/afterHoursOf leaves greetingAudioUrl out of the patch. So sameAs(patch.afterHours, current.afterHours) is false, and `!current?.afterHours` is also false because it is an object. The 'echoed' filter in assist.js line 444 never drops it. Fix: run current.afterHours through afterHoursOf before comparing, or treat 'disabled with no options' on both sides as echoed.

readiness.stillNeeded says 'Key 4: This key texts the caller, but you have no Texting Number yet' even though key 4 has smsFrom mn_ab01, Alice owns that Texting Number, and the IVR saves without error. The context the frontend sends has textingNumbers: [] and textingOn: false, so the readiness check doesn't see the eSIM-line texting number. The chat's own 'missing' list no longer shows this, so it only reaches users through readiness.

In preview, the typed Replay/Decline message is not used or stored. Fine for a dry run, but there is no way to confirm the live message there. The live path (resolveOtp message) is covered only by unit tests.

issues: The row stays on one line, but the name input ('Name, e.g. A…') and phone input ('+141555501…') are squeezed, so their placeholders are cut off. The side 'Call flow' column takes the space. Consider a min width for the phone input, or a narrower action select.
It covers the top of the page content, including the IVR form while you preview it. Acceptable, since 'Answer later' hides it.

action_items: Emily IVR assist: normalise current.afterHours (and extensions) with the same cleaner before the sameAs echo check. Then an untouched afterHours {enabled:false, greetingAudioUrl:null, options:[]} doesn't produce summary lines, the 'Hours schedule' missing note or the 'After-hours menu' chip.
Emily readiness: add eSIM/Texting Numbers (e.g. mn_ab01) to context.textingNumbers, or check smsFrom against the account's lines, so key 4 isn't flagged with 'no Texting Number yet'.
Optional: give the Extensions phone input a min width at 1280 so placeholders aren't cut off.
critical_code_review_comments: OtpAlerts hides by `${id}:${attempt}`, and Replay keeps the attempt, so the same key comes back after a Replay. In testing the banner reappeared correctly when the new code arrived (verified on Quick IVR). Still, keep the key unique per code (e.g. include the holdEndsAt/code) so a Replay never matches an already-hidden key.

Decide keeps the typed message in local state. When the banner remounts for the next code, the box goes back to the key's default replayMessage, so a live edit doesn't carry over between replays. That may be intended.
The confirm-preview view is one very long line (ivr-connections.js line 34). Hard to review; split it into a helper.

success_rate.backend: 100% (11/11 pytest; node unit tests ivr_more_keys and fax_ivr_doc_sweep pass)
